quests.title: The Quiet Carriage, Burwood
quests.blurb: The quiet carriage runs on shame and somebody on the ten past five out of Burwood has stopped feeling it. Ride it, see the crime, and apply the shame manually.

apply the shame manually

quests.title: The Wiley Park Shortcut
quests.blurb: Every courier has a route that is not on a map and mine goes through Wiley Park. They have started locking one end. Go and find out whether it is locked forever or just locked today.

steps.label: the end they lock
the long way round, so you understand what it costs

the two arguing over the grass

quests.title: Whatever Is Under the Grey at Westmead

quests.title: The Hill Above Rozelle Bay
quests.blurb: There is a bench on the hill above Rozelle Bay I have watched from a moving bus about fourteen thousand times. I am not going to stop — that is not the kind of person I turned out to be. So you go, at twenty past four, when the light is worth it.

steps.label: up the hill, the way the road does not go
the view I have never stopped for

quests.blurb: Done at Glenfield on grand final week for something that is only an offence if a sign says so, and I am the only one who seems to have noticed. How do you photograph a thing not being somewhere? That is your problem now.

steps.label: where the sign is supposed to be
photograph the absence, which is harder than it sounds
the one who tells you photography is not allowed here

quests.title: The Strip Outside Carramar
quests.blurb: Nobody planted the strip at Carramar. I did, on the long weekend, at half six, so nobody would ask. I would like the fifteenth to go badly for council.

steps.label: the strip, which is a garden now
the man with the whipper snipper
photograph it while it still exists

quests.title: Night Fill, Homebush
quests.blurb: Ten to six, nobody in the building but us and a radio that gets one station. Somebody has been taking things and they know our roster, which means they come in off the late train at Homebush.

steps.label: come in on the late one like they do
the loading door nobody watches
whoever is standing in it at two in the morning
$39 of what they took, back

quests.title: The Window Above Pendle Hill
quests.blurb: 16 years above Pendle Hill. I do not hear the trains any more, which means I hear it instantly when one of them is wrong. Since Thursdays the joins sound different.

steps.label: ride it and listen to the joins
photograph the stretch that sounds wrong
tell me I am not mad

quests.title: Setting Up at Narara
quests.blurb: 19 years in the Narara market. The bays are not allocated, they are *known*, and since every second Friday somebody has decided that knowing does not count, and nobody upstairs wants to hear it.

steps.label: the bays, at the hour it happens
the bloke with the extra trestle
you will want one at that hour

quests.title: The Clock at Lakemba
quests.blurb: Somebody set the Lakemba clock that way on purpose and everyone who knows why is nearly gone. The old crew drink near Wiley Park on the first of the month. Go and ask, and it has been like that since the merge.

steps.label: the clock, four minutes fast, for the file
to Wiley Park, where the old crew drink

quests.title: The Dog at Lindfield
quests.blurb: A dog meets the 5:40 at Lindfield every weekday and nobody gets off for it. Four months of this. I have decided it is not going to be a sad story. Find out whose it is.

steps.label: the end of the platform, at twenty to six
the street it walks home to
tell me it is not a sad story

quests.title: The Book at Wollstonecraft
quests.blurb: I run a small book on things that are not races — weather, delays, whether the twenty past four out of Wollstonecraft runs on time. Somebody is beating it by information, not luck. Ride the run they ride.

steps.label: ride the run they ride
the two who follow you off it

quests.title: Last Service out of Macquarie Park
quests.blurb: The last one through Macquarie Park carries four people and one of them is always asleep. Ride it to Macquarie University, photograph the platform with nobody on it, and come back and tell me the place still exists when there is no one in it.

the empty platform, lit and pointless
